content: Pyridoxine, also known as vitamin B6, is essential for your body to properly utilize energy from the food you consume, produce red blood cells, and ensure the proper functioning of your nervous system. It is prescribed to treat and prevent vitamin B6 deficiency, which may result from inadequate dietary intake, certain medications, or specific medical conditions. In some cases, pyridoxine may be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Pyridoxine is available in regular and extended-release (long-acting) tablet forms. It is typically taken once daily. Follow the instructions provided on your prescription or package label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take pyridoxine exactly as directed. Do not take more or less than prescribed, and do not take it more frequently than instructed by your doctor. Extended-release tablets should be swallowed whole; do not chew, crush, or cut them. Before taking pyridoxine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to pyridoxine or any other medications. Additionally, provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially levodopa (Larodopa, Sinemet), phenobarbital, phenytoin (Dilantin), and other vitamins. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking pyridoxine, contact your doctor immediately. Your doctor may recommend increasing your intake of foods rich in vitamin B6, such as whole-grain cereals, fish, vegetables, beans, liver, and other organ meats. If you miss a dose of pyridoxine, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Pyridoxine may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: upset stomach, headache, drowsiness, or sensations of tingling, prickling, burning, or tightness in the hands and feet. Store pyridoxine in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on the safe disposal of medications. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as your doctor may order tests to monitor your response to pyridoxine. Do not share your medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
